setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Wharf Rat** (2 reviews): Singled out with Cold Rain, Chinatown Shuffle, Jack Straw, Looks Like Rain, Big Boss Man and El Paso as delightful; Very mellow, laid-back version [11][15]
- **Loser** (1 review): The audience tape has a recording error less than thirty seconds into the song [4]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Slower than usual with great groove; Phil sings harmony instead of Donna, and Jerry sounds like pedal steel [10]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Played full-throttle and loud, but reviewer finds it musically dull [14]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Mix is slightly more evenly balanced than the official release, with Weir prominent and Garcia less buried [9]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Keith stretches out on Playin' and Truckin'; the jams are blazing, though they space out at times [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-03-26.133303.sbd.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 208 min; rated 4.57/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the band's sound system was loud and overly clean; Miller's remix is clear but could use warmth [14]
- **gd72-03-26.aud.hanno.15413.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 12 songs; 80 min; rated 1.33/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has more crowd noise than band, and an error in the recording appears shortly after Loser begins; Audience recording sounds terrible, as if taped from inside a toilet tank or restroom; Audience recording is awful; reviewer says no decent recording circulates, only an uncirculated soundboard [4][6][7][8]
- **gd1972-03-26.136689.sbd.sirmick.flac1648**: soundboard; 26 songs; 203 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer heard the uncirculated soundboard on Sirius satellite radio's Grateful Dead channel, describing it as energetic with breathtaking moments [7]
- Jerry Moore's audience tape from 03-25 is the best of the Academy run, though still below typical early '70s quality [8]
- Reviewer found the E72 releases somewhat Jerry-centric, whereas this show's official release puts Weir up front [9]
- Reviewer says this is where 1972 starts sounding amazing [11]
- Show offers a glimpse of the Europe '72 sound without Donna's vocals present [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-03-26.133303.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k) [1]. Also: David Gans helped remove many flaws using soundBlade; some flaws may remain, and disc changes are seamless [1]
- **gd72-03-26.aud.hanno.15413.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience [3]
- **gd1972-03-26.136689.sbd.sirmick.flac1648**: taped by Anonomous; transferred by SIRMick; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source: sbd > master reel > dat (48k) [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by johnsdeadart.blogspot.com: [John's Custom Grateful Dead Album Cover Art](https://johnsdeadart.blogspot.com/2017/05/blog-post_90.html) [17]
- Fan art by johnsdeadart.blogspot.com: [John's Custom Grateful Dead Album Cover Art](https://johnsdeadart.blogspot.com/2017/05/blog-post_90.html) [18]
